body: Is this correct? The previous logic found the property and returned it, but now, after removing `return`, a property with the same name can be found multiple times, and the base class definition will overwrite the child class definition. Maybe the method should be called in reverse order, from the most distant ancestor to the current class?

Why did you move the call from the next loop? Doesn't that mean `validate_property()` will now be called from the last property to the first (plus it won't be called for the class category added below)?
This is correct. The method is multilevel, so it should be called for every class in hierarchy, starting with the deepest one. See the documentation.
`validate_property()` is supposed to be called only for class' properties, not the dynamic ones from `_get_property_list()`. The order does not really matter.

I was about to make a PR to change the documentation to the [actual beavior](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs/pull/11757) on the correct repo but found this PR.

For me there is no exception, the `_validate_property()` is called for properties added by `_get_property_list()`. And I am using it so I hope it's a feature not a bug.

It's a bug.
Also validating properties from `_get_property_list()` is redundant, because you already make them from scratch.

This is not true if you want to validate property added by a plugin. Like when you extend a plugin class who add properties from the `_get_property_list` method. You can't call `super()` in `_get_property_list()` right ?

Yeah, you can customize properties added by `_get_property_list()` in parent class. But it's the same in core classes, so scripting should be consistent. If a plugin is expected to have its properties customized, it shouldn't expose them via property list. Feel free to open a proposal I guess.
